paragraphs.text: Reversing Harlow's margin decline
Margin plan for the board meeting, February 2027
Harlow Fresh Markets
CEO, presenting to the board
Synthetic benchmark data: the company and every figure are fictional

slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Which actions should Harlow take, and in what order, to lift its operating margin from 1.0% in FY2025 to at least 3.0% by FY2028, within $25M of one-time cost?
Where did the margin go, and how much must the plan deliver?
How much gross margin can promotions and private label win back?
Should Harlow cut store hours, and what would it do to shrink?
What should Harlow do about home delivery and its weakest stores?
Which actions come first, and does the plan meet the board's tests?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO, presenting the margin plan to the board for approval

Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028; At most $25M of one-time cost or capital over FY2026–FY2028; Operating income of at least $20M in FY2026 (lender covenant); No early closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote; Home delivery kept in some form
Board meeting, February 2027
Exiting home delivery entirely (owners' commitment); New stores and remodels; Refinancing or renegotiating the covenant

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Fix promotions, store routines and delivery fees and close nine weak stores, not cut hours across the board: about 3.2% by FY2028
The margin fell from 3.4% to 1.0% through gross margin and e-commerce, not mainly wages
–	Gross margin and e-commerce caused 79% of the fall; the 3.0% target needs about $30M more a year
Dropping money-losing promotions adds up to $10.5M a year and private label $4.1M more
–	38% of FY2025 promotion events lost money; deeper promotions have not stopped losses near ValuMart
Fix routines where hours are fewest and trim hours only where most: about $7.0M, not an 8% cut
–	Store labor caused 13% of the fall; a chain-wide cut could lose up to two-thirds to shrink
Repricing delivery recovers $2.5M of a $10.4M online loss; closing nine stores adds $6.6M
–	The average home delivery loses about $12; six of the nine stores can close at lease end
Seven actions reach about 3.2% for $7.5M one-time if promotions hold; quick wins go first
–	The 2027 wage rise, up to $7.3M a year, would cut that to 2.7%, so reserve levers are needed
